extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS authors, reviewers, area chairs, program chairs, and the machine learning research community (people involved in conference peer review)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance, forms, and standards used in the NeurIPS 2021 peer-review process, including reviewer and meta-review forms, the NeurIPS author checklist, and the experiment's procedural acceptance rules. Focused on evaluating and making accept/reject decisions for NeurIPS submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (reviewer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary* Briefly summarize the paper and its contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred field (mandatory). Short synopsis that captures main contributions; used to ground the rest of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main Review (originality, quality, clarity, significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Main Review* Provide a full review of the submission, including its originality, quality, clarity, and significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred field (mandatory). Reviewers are referred to https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2021/Reviewer-Guidelines for guidance on questions to address; reviewers may use Markdown/LaTeX. Should be a full assessment that justifies scores and critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations And Societal Impact (authors/responders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations And Societal Impact* Have the authors adequately addressed the limitations and potential negative societal impact of their work? If not, please include constructive suggestions for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred field (mandatory). Reviewers should check whether authors have acknowledged limitations and any potential negative impacts, and provide constructive suggestions where missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Concerns (reviewer description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical Concerns If there are ethical issues with this paper, please describe them and the extent to which they have been acknowledged or addressed by the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should describe ethical issues and reference the NeurIPS Ethics Guidelines (link provided). This field supports decisions about whether to send the paper to ethics review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needs Ethics Review (yes/no)
rubrics_metrics.description: Needs Ethics Review* Should this paper be sent for ethics review? Options: Yes / No
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred field (mandatory). Used to flag papers that require an ethics reviewer; reviewers should use Ethical Concerns field to justify flagging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics Review Area (areas of expertise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics Review Area If you flagged this paper for ethics review, what area of expertise would it be most useful for the ethics reviewer to have?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options to select (click all that apply): Discrimination / Bias / Fairness Concerns; Inadequate Data and Algorithm Evaluation; Inappropriate Potential Applications & Impact; Privacy and Security; Legal Compliance; Research Integrity Issues; Responsible Research Practice; I don't know. Helps match ethics reviewers to papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Spent Reviewing (effort)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time Spent Reviewing* How much time did you spend reviewing this paper (in hours)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred field (mandatory). Captures reviewer effort and can be used for analysis of review quality/costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating / Overall score (10 to 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rating* Please provide an "overall score" for this submission. Options: 10: Top 5% of accepted NeurIPS papers, seminal paper; 9: Top 15% of accepted NeurIPS papers, strong accept; 8: Top 50% of accepted NeurIPS papers, clear accept; 7: Good paper, accept; 6: Marginally above the acceptance threshold; 5: Marginally below the acceptance threshold; 4: Ok but not good enough - rejection; 3: Clear rejection; 2: Strong rejection; 1: Trivial or wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred field (mandatory). Provides explicit anchors tying numerical scores to relative rankings among accepted papers; reviewers should justify the chosen rating in their Main Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence (reviewer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidence* Please provide a "confidence score" for your assessment of this submission. Options: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment... 4: You are confident... 3: You are fairly confident... 2: You are willing to defend your assessment... 1: Your assessment is an educated guess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred field (mandatory). Detailed descriptions indicate how familiar the reviewer is with related work and how carefully details (math/etc.) were checked; used to weight reviewer judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct affirmation (reviewer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code of Conduct* (Checkbox) While performing my duties as a reviewer (including writing reviews and participating in discussions), I have and will continue to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred field (mandatory). Formal attestation to expected behavior while reviewing and participating in discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review Recommendation (AC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation* Please recommend a decision for this submission. Options: Accept (Oral); Accept (Spotlight); Accept (Poster); Reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred field (mandatory). ACs must choose one of the decision categories; these feed into program chair/senior area chair deliberations and final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review Confidence / bumpability (AC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidence* Please qualify your recommendation. Options: You are absolutely certain.; This decision can be bumped up (e.g., you are recommending to accept this paper as a poster but it would also make a fine spotlight).; This decision can be bumped down (e.g., you have a preference for accepting this paper as a poster but you wouldn’t mind if it is rejected).; You are not certain what the right decision should be. This is a submission you wish to discuss further with the SAC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred field (mandatory). ACs indicate certainty and whether the decision may be adjusted in calibration; these 'can be bumped up/down' labels are used in analyses of consistency and when shifting thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review text / justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Metareview* Please provide a meta-review for this submission. Your meta-review should explain your decision to the authors. Your comments should augment the reviews, and explain how the reviews, author response, and discussion were used to arrive at your decision. If you want to make a decision that is not clearly supported by the reviews, perhaps because the reviewers did not come to a consensus, please justify your decision appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred field (mandatory). AC meta-reviews must explain decision rationale, link evidence from reviews/response/discussion, and justify deviations from reviewer consensus when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review History (AC data collection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review History* Have you previously reviewed or area chaired (a version of) this work for another archival venue? (This information is only requested in order to collect aggregate statistics for NeurIPS 2021. Your response will not be shared with authors or reviewers, nor will it affect the submission’s chance of acceptance.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred field (mandatory for aggregate data only). Used for conference statistics; not used in public decision rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider For An Award (AC checkbox)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider For An Award (Checkbox) Yes, this paper should be seriously considered for an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional checkbox for ACs to flag outstanding papers for awards consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: NeurIPS paper checklist — general author items
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. For all authors... (a) Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? [Yes] (b) Did you describe the limitations of your work? [Yes] (c) Did you discuss any potential negative societal impacts of your work? [Yes] (d) Have you read the ethics review guidelines and ensured that your paper conforms to them? [Yes]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should confirm these items when submitting. The checklist promotes responsible research practices and makes authors explicitly consider claims, limitations, societal impact, and adherence to ethics guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: NeurIPS paper checklist — theoretical results
rubrics_metrics.description: 2. If you are including theoretical results... (a) Did you state the full set of assumptions of all theoretical results? [N/A] (b) Did you include complete proofs of all theoretical results? [N/A]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors with theoretical contributions should state assumptions and include full proofs (or provide pointers). Mark N/A where not relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: NeurIPS paper checklist — experimental reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: 3. If you ran experiments... (a) Did you include the code, data, and instructions needed to reproduce the main experimental results (either in the supplemental material or as a URL)? [No]. (b) Did you specify all the training details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen)? [N/A]. (c) Did you report error bars (e.g., with respect to the random seed after running experiments multiple times)? [Yes]. (d) Did you include the total amount of compute and the type of resources used? [No].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should include code/data and detailed experimental protocol to enable reproducibility where possible. The checklist acknowledges possible constraints (e.g., privacy) and asks authors to report error bars and compute details where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: NeurIPS paper checklist — use of existing assets
rubrics_metrics.description: 4. If you are using existing assets (e.g., code, data, models) or curating/releasing new assets... (a) If your work uses existing assets, did you cite the creators? [N/A]. (b) Did you mention the license of the assets? [N/A]. (c) Did you include any new assets either in the supplemental material or as a URL? [N/A]. (d) Did you discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose data you’re using/curating? [Yes]. (e) Did you discuss whether the data you are using/curating contains personally identifiable information or offensive content? [Yes].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must disclose asset provenance, licensing when applicable, consent procedures, and whether datasets include PII or offensive content; IRB/consent notes are required where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: NeurIPS paper checklist — crowdsourcing & human subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: 5. If you used crowdsourcing or conducted research with human subjects... (a) Did you include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable? [Yes]. (b) Did you describe any potential participant risks, with links to Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals, if applicable? [Yes]. (c) Did you include the estimated hourly wage paid to participants and the total amount spent on participant compensation? [Yes].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must provide participant instructions, describe participant risks and IRB links, and state compensation details when human subjects/crowdsourcing are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicated-papers acceptance rule (experiment procedural standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplicated papers were accepted if at least one of the two copies was recommended for acceptance and no “fatal flaw” was found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational rule for the NeurIPS 2021 consistency experiment. Examples of a "fatal flaw" include an error in a major result that cannot easily be fixed. In two cases where committees disagreed about fatality, papers were conditionally accepted with conditions jointly determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment constraints for duplicated papers (experiment)
rubrics_metrics.description: During assignment we assigned two ACs and twice the usual number of reviewers to duplicated papers and split ACs/reviewers at random between the two copies. We ensured the two ACs were assigned to different SACs and any newly invited reviewer for one copy was added as a conflict for the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural safeguards intended to keep the two committees independent and avoid overlap; relevant as a standard for running randomized controlled experiments on peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC 'can be bumped up/down' label (used in calibration & analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: When ACs entered recommendations, they were asked to note whether they were sure or whether the paper could be bumped up or down (e.g., "This decision can be bumped up" / "can be bumped down").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These labels are used during calibration and in analyses (e.g., treating some poster/reject pairs as consistent). They capture AC uncertainty about the decision frontier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer guidance / referential standard
rubrics_metrics.description: See https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2021/Reviewer-Guidelines for guidance on questions to address in your review, and faq for how to incorporate Markdown and LaTeX into your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are explicitly pointed to a separate set of reviewer guidelines; the Main Review field refers reviewers to that document for detailed evaluative guidance.
